programmes.d: High tech is revolutionizing the way art is being created.
Plastic is one of mankind’s most revolutionary inventions.
By 2050, astronauts may be using 3D printers to build homes on other planets.
We all have DNA, and it’s being used for a lot more than solving crimes.

Ash Creek is the site of the most recent recorded meteorite fall in United States (February 15, 2009). In this episode, Geoff and Steve will follow clues provided by the locals to uncover the mysterious rocks of this fall.

In 1995, Professor Jim Kriegh discovered a field of of ancient stone meteorites; the Gold Basin Meteorite is known as the best mapped strewn field in history. In this episode, Geoff and Steve get exclusive access to hunt meteorites in uncharted areas.

In Canada, Geoff and search for pieces of the Buzzard Coulee Meteorite. Also, the meteorite hunters receive a surprise invitation to visit the newly discovered, and highly protected, Whitecourt Crater and hunt the surrounding area.

Dry lake beds are a great place to find never before discovered meteorites. In this episode, the terrain of the bed provides spectacular visuals and high-speed action as Geoff and Steve cover as much ground as possible, looking for dark rocks.
Building for God reached a high point in the Middle Ages with Notre Dame.
Temples, designed to honor the Gods, have been at the heart of cities since earliest times.
Without water, civilization is simply not possible; Romans took control of their water seriously.
As far back as the Bronze Age, humans were building ships capable of crossing oceans and trading.

Earth has an evil twin. Venus. It is shrouded in a lethal atmosphere of carbon dioxide and acid rain. The surface temperature is hot enough to melt lead and the pressure high enough to crush a nuclear submarine.

The Earth is built to last. It is a 4,550,000,000-year-old, 5,973,600,000,000,000,000,000-tonne ball of rock and iron. It has taken more devastating asteroid hits in its lifetime than you've had hot dinners, and it still orbits happily around the sun.
By far the largest planet, 1300 times the size of Earth, it’s a world so enormous it could swallow every planet and moon in the solar system and still have room to spare.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Inner Worlds
programmes.d: They orbit between our planet and our star. Mercury and Venus make up half of our terrestrial planets, but we still know very little about them. As we take a closer look at our companions, we find more questions than answers.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Next Stop Mars
programmes.d: Mars has fired our imagination for thousands of years. The tantilizing possibility of life has made it the most inviting planet in our solar system. It is the only other place that man may one day call home.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Planet Makers
programmes.d: From the beginnings of our solar system 4.5 billions years ago, there remain many clues to reveal its evolution. Remnant debris, asteroids, and comets are what's left of the building blocks to our celestial neighborhood.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Gas Giants
programmes.d: In the cold, dark expanse of our solar system, beyond the asteroid belt, lie the giant planets. Some can be seen with the naked eye, others have been visited by our camera. What secrets do they hold?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Moons of Olympus
programmes.d: There are many more worlds in our solar system than just the planets. The mysterious moons of the gas giants may hold much more than we ever imagined. Each one is unique, and each one deserves a scrutinous eye.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Sun
programmes.d: The sun bathes our planet in warmth and light. It powers the machinery of nature, our weather, and it encourages and sustains life on land and at sea. We study it closely, and it can reveal the secrets of all other stars.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Exo Planets
programmes.d: As scientists and astronomers peer more closely and with evermore fidelity at nearby stars, they are discovering countless exo planets. How many Earth-like planets are out there? Could one of them hold life not so different from our own?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Edge of the Universe
programmes.d: The night sky is a time machine. The further we look out into the universe, the further back in time we reach. Most of what we see is actually dark matter and dark energy, but its nature eludes us ... for the moment.
The ringed planet is of immense interest to researchers who believe that Saturn's ring system will share similarities with the proto-planetary disc.
Currently the only destination for Astronauts and Cosmonauts is the orbiting research platform known as the International Space Station.
The solar system's largest planet has been visited by automated probes since the 1970s.
Before spaceflight aviators began wearing pressure suits to allow them to function at higher ceilings.
The Sun is our star. Its energy enables life on the Earth to thrive yet we know so little about the solar weather and the 11 year solar cycle.
Space telescopes orbiting above the distorting effects of the Earth's atmosphere, such as the Hubble, have made incredible contributions to our knowledge of the universe.
There are so many unanswered questions about the stars, the galaxies and the universe and just mapping what lies in the night sky is immensely difficult.
As our expertise in space technology increases there have been spin-offs in many areas: particularly in communications.
The world of soft robotics, where robots are so human-like they can actually feel things.
The STEM initiative is getting a big boost from both the private, and public, sectors.
Chuck Pell has a conversation in real-time with a hologram of a holocaust survivor.
Future tech is changing the basics of human existence, including our five senses.
Sustainability is a word you’re going to hear a lot more of on the road to 2050.
